title: Compliance scout — control cartography (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Rapid, informal sketch for control mapping and risk questions related to SOC2 readiness for Redwood Private and Dedicated offerings. Not a final artifact — use as a working checklist to surface discussion points for the trust ops sync.

Context / background (short):
- Past quarter: dedicated customers asked for clearer evidence of segregation (Dedicated) and customer-managed keys (Private). Ops team ran an intake audit (see JIRA SEC-412) and found gaps in documented key rotation and change control for compiled inference kernels. We need a lightweight mapping to TSC categories to prioritize work.

High-level objectives for this doc:
1) List candidate controls (rough phrasing) that we can plausibly evidence within 30–60 days.
2) Map each candidate to the most relevant SOC2/Trust Services Criteria (TSC) buckets (CC6, CC7, CC3 style — use shorthand for now).
3) Surface open questions and blockers (owners + suggested next step).
4) Create a short prioritized TODO list for next week: owners, quick wins, dependencies.

Quick risk sketch (brain dump):
- Key-management drift: multiple teams touching KMS policies, inconsistent labels in cloud accounts. Risk: unauthorized key reuse or delayed rotation.
- Model artifact provenance: model binaries pulled from open model catalog; need better SBOM-like inventory for model weights. Risk: inability to trace a model version when responding to a customer incident.
- Deployment rollback gaps: we have canary flows in Redwood Console, but audit trail for automatic fallback events sometimes lacks operator context. Risk: incomplete incident timeline for audits.
- Access sprawl: ephemeral admin tokens created by infra automation with long TTLs. Risk: excessive blast radius.

Candidate controls (phrases for now) + mapping notes:
1) "Central KMS policy baseline and rotation cadence" -> TSC: CC6 (logical & physical access) / CC7 (change management). Notes: baseline should include labeling convention, rotation schedule, and automated alerts for TTL > X days. Evidence: KMS policy snapshot, rotation logs, pager alerts.

2) "Model artifact inventory (lightweight SBOM)" -> TSC: CC3 (system operations) / CC5 (system and communication). Notes: track origin URL, model hash, quant config, applied patches. Evidence: CSV export + periodic verification job output.

3) "Rollback events: annotated operator notes" -> TSC: CC4 (change monitoring) / CC3. Notes: patch the Console to require optional free-text reason for auto-fallbacks and link to ticket id. Evidence: Console event export + ticket link.

4) "Ephemeral token TTL policy and automated revocation" -> TSC: CC6. Notes: find all automation flows that request long-lived tokens (Terraform, infra pipelines). Evidence: token audit log and a short remediation plan.

5) "Isolation checklist for Dedicated capacity onboarding" -> TSC: CC5 / CC6. Notes: network ACL baseline, dedicated VPC network tests, and customer data routing notes. Evidence: onboarding checklist + post-onboard verification runbook.

Unresolved questions (need research / owners):
- Where do we currently store the model origin/hash metadata? (Owner suggestion: Applied ML / model-onboarding team)
- Can we add a lightweight SBOM hook to the model ingestion pipeline without blocking onboarding flow? (Owner: Applied ML + Serving Runtime)
- How frequent are Terraform runs that create tokens longer than 7 days? Quick query: infra-logs -> identify top 10 creators. (Owner: Platform Engineering / Infra)
- Which Redwood Console endpoints already include a free-text field we can reuse for annotated operator notes? (Owner: Console & Rollouts)

Quick queries to run (for next sync) — prioritized:
- Q1: list all KMS keys tagged with "redwood:purpose" != "prod" and last-rotated > 90 days. (Owner: Lina) — due 2026-02-18
- Q2: run a one-off inventory of model files in S3 (or storage) -> return: origin URL, sha256, upload timestamp. (Owner: Ethan) — due 2026-02-20
- Q3: Console export: last 90 days of auto-fallback events, fields: timestamp, route, model, operator_id (if any), fallback_reason. (Owner: Amaya) — due 2026-02-19

Low-effort quick wins (30–60 days):
- Add tag enforcement to KMS creation via Terraform guardrails (policy + pre-commit check).
- Add a job that writes a small JSON SBOM alongside each model upload (no blocking latency).
- Add a small Console UX change to require a ticket link on manual rollback (toggleable).

Action items / owners (short):
- Amaya: draft a 1-pager for Sec Ops (1 page + attachments) summarizing the 5 candidate controls (due 2026-02-21).
- Lina: run KMS rotation query + share top 5 stale keys (due 2026-02-18).
- Ethan: prototype SBOM writer in model ingestion (POC branch, include test file) (due 2026-02-24).
- Console team (Liaison: TBD): feasibility doc for adding free-text operator note (due 2026-03-01).

Notes-to-self / heuristics (scratch):
- Keep evidence lightweight where possible: auditors accept scripted exports if they are repeatable.
- Prioritize controls that also reduce developer toil (dual benefit sells faster).
- Avoid big reworks before mapping: auditors prefer an incremental plan with milestones.

Risk prioritization (one-liner):
- Tier 1 (urgent): KMS rotation + ephem token TTLs. High impact and relatively small work.
- Tier 2: Model provenance (bigger lift but long-term important).
- Tier 3: Console annotated notes + onboarding checklist (process + UX work).

Conversation seeds for trust ops sync (use these as Slack prompts):
- "Quick check: do we have an SBOM equivalent for model weights? If not, can we ship a 1-liner metadata file on upload?"
- "I'd like a small dashboard showing token creators and TTLs > 7d — who's the best owner to add that?"

References / pointers (for later):
- Confluence seed page: SECURITY/SOC2-INIT-87 (linked above)
- JIRA ticket: SEC-412 (inventory + intake report)
- Infra query examples: infra-logs -> token-ttl-report (ask infra-eng for exact script)

Final thoughts (scratch):
- This doc should morph into a proper control mapping table later (CSV or sheet) — but only after we validate the SBOM and KMS queries. For now, keep small and opinionated.

-- end scratch --

[notes: I try to leave commentary markers and short prompts so others can jump in; make this doc the starting point for the 15m pre-sync review.]
